messages:
hana_docs: quick one — i'm preparing a short example for the audit-log docs that shows a safe, public-friendly flow: redact a sensitive field, then place the redacted entry on hold during a retention migration. want to avoid legalese and avoid implying we can restore redacted data. @lee_security @james_legal any quick flags?

lee_security: good idea. two quick asks: (1) use 'preserve under hold' or 'pause automated deletion' phrasing; (2) explicitly say redaction is irreversible from the retrievable record (don't say 'permanent' in a way that confuses backups). also mention KMS if customer-managed.

james_legal: legal okay with that. add a single-line: 'Removal of a hold resumes normal retention rules from that moment.' Also note holds and redactions are auditable.

sam_eng: i'll draft the minimal snippets (curl + python) — public-safe: bearer auth + endpoint + payload. plan: POST /v1/audit/redact -> returns redacted_log_id, then POST /v1/audit/holds to preserve it. keep examples compact.

hana_docs: draft text i plan to add:

"Plain language: To remove sensitive fields but still preserve the event, redact the fields and then place the redacted entry on legal hold. Redaction removes the sensitive content from the retrievable audit record and is not reversible from the dashboard. Applying a hold pauses automated deletion for the preserved entry until an authorized person removes it; when a hold is released, normal retention rules resume."

hana_docs: snippet (public-friendly):

```
# 1) redact sensitive fields
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/audit/redact \  -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" \  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \  -d '{"log_id":"l-200","redact_fields":["request.body.credit_card"]}'# response -> { "redacted_log_id": "l-200.redacted" }

# 2) preserve the redacted entry
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/audit/holds \  -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" \  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \  -d '{"log_id":"l-200.redacted","action":"apply","reason":"migration - case 99"}'```

```python
# check: python example for release
import requests
r = requests.post(
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/audit/holds",
  headers={"Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN"},
  json={"log_id": "l-200.redacted", "action": "release", "reason": "case closed"}
)
print(r.status_code)  # 200
```

hana_docs: short bullets under examples: "Requires roles: `audit:redact` and `audit:hold`. Redaction removes the sensitive content from the retrievable record; the preserved (held) entry contains the redacted payload. Held entries pause TTL-based purges but still count toward storage quotas and backups. When customer-managed KMS is enabled, held entries are encrypted with the customer's key. Holds and redaction actions are recorded in the audit trail (actor + timestamp)."

lee_security: nit: change 'pause automated deletion' -> 'pause TTL-based purges' to align with other pages. add parenthetical "(does not change backup lifecycle)".

james_legal: LGTM with that nit. :thumbsup:
